about: Conduit's rich cards: the one definition both the conduit_push plugin and Conduit read. Conduit ships a byte-identical copy (Conduit/Cards/card-schema.json) and its CI fails when the copy differs from this file on main. 'card' is a JSON Schema subset (type, enum, properties, required, items, minItems, maxItems, maxLength, minimum, maximum, format uri or line) that goes into the tool definitions as is, except that tools take a diff card's diff as 'inputs.diff' (a patch, a patch file or two texts), which the plugin reads into the card's diff, and a review card's review as 'inputs.review' (options with their pages), which the plugin keeps on the host and reads into the card's review. Text is cleaned the same way everywhere: control characters become spaces, and the invisible ones that can make text read differently from what it holds (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069, U+200B, U+2060 and U+FEFF) are dropped, except in a line, where each becomes U+FFFD so it shows. A line (format line) keeps its spaces: it is cut to maxLength, but it is never trimmed. Normalizing is the same on both sides: unknown keys are dropped, text is cleaned and cut to maxLength, an invalid optional value is dropped, an invalid list item is dropped, and an invalid required value makes its object invalid. Before that, a table's cells (and its column names) are made text: a string stays as it is, an empty one or anything that isn't text or a number becomes –, and a number becomes its digits (a whole number with no decimal point, otherwise the shortest form that reads back as the same number). Then the rules in 'rules' apply. 'board' holds the shared definitions of a whole conduit_show call's layout and next, which tools offer beside the cards. cards/card-vectors.json holds the shared examples both test suites run.
rules: A card keeps only its own type's field (places for map, place and places; people for contact; stats, chart, weather, options, steps, media, status, table, timeline, checklist, list, progress, callout, diff, review or sections for the others), plus title, live and actions, source on every type but map, place and places, needs on steps and ranked on list; a card without its type's field is dropped.
A route is kept only on a map card, only when every place given survived, when 'to' (and 'from' if given) name places in the list, and when 'from' differs from 'to'.
A place card keeps only its first place.
A place's or person's photo is kept only when its url is https.
A chart keeps only the series with one value per label; a pie keeps only its first series, and no value of a pie may be negative. A chart with no series left is dropped.
A weather card needs a source and at least one of now, hours or days (an empty list counts as none); a day whose low is above its high is dropped.
A comparison keeps only its first recommended option.
A media card needs a source and keeps only items whose url is https (dropped when none is left); artwork is kept only when it is https, and an image keeps no duration or artwork.

A contact's phone is kept only when it holds 3 to 20 digits and nothing but digits, spaces and + - ( ) . characters; an email only when it is one address like name@example.com, with no spaces, quotes, brackets, commas, semicolons, colons or any of ? # % & =.
A person's message is kept only when their phone is.
A table keeps only the rows with one cell per column, and is dropped when none is left.
A checklist keeps only the first item with a given text, compared without regard to case.
A list item's photo is kept only when its url is https.
A progress item is kept only when its goal is above 0 and its value is 0 or more.
A diff file keeps only the hunk lines that start with +, - or a space, and a hunk with none left is dropped; a binary file keeps no hunks.
A diff's id is kept only when it is cd- and 16 hex digits.
Only the first card in a set keeps a given live name.

An element keeps only its own kind's fields: text and role for text; value, label and change for metric; text for badge; symbol for icon; url and label for image; progress and label for progress; nothing for divider; id, input, label, value, lines, options, min, max and placeholder for field; the button fields (label, action, id, target, symbol, style and confirm) for button; and tone on text, metric, badge, icon and progress. An element without its kind's own (text for text and badge, value for metric, symbol for icon, url for image, progress for progress, id and input for field, label and action for button) is dropped, and a section with none left is dropped.
An image element is kept only when its url is https.

A field is dropped when its id, label or placeholder names a secret: read after NFKC normalization (so full-width letters read as their ASCII forms) in lower case with everything but letters (of any script) and digits as spaces, its words joined together hold password, passcode, secret, token, apikey, onetime, privatekey, recoverykey, licensekey, seedphrase, verificationcode, securitycode, authcode, backupcode, passphrase, totp, masterkey, credential, 2fa, twofactor, logincode, accesscode, unlockcode, securitykey, resetcode, recoverycode, activationcode, authkey, verificationkey or backupkey, or the same in another language (passwort, kennwort, contraseña, motdepasse, senha, пароль, hasło, şifre, katasandi, パスワード, 暗証番号, 認証コード, 密码, 密碼, 验证码, 驗證碼, 비밀번호, 인증번호, 인증코드, bestätigungscode, verifizierungscode, zugangscode, códigodeverificación, codigodeverificacion, códigodeverificação, codedevérification, codedeverification, codicediverifica, kodeverifikasi, doğrulamakodu, kodweryfikacyjny, кодподтверждения, clavedeacceso or contrasena), or one of its words is pin, otp, cvv, cvc, mfa, pincode or mfacode (a word also splitting where ASCII letters and digits meet another script's letters, so PIN码 reads as pin), when the card already has a field with that id, or when the card already has six fields. lines and placeholder go with text, options with choice, min and max with number. A choice field keeps only the first option with a given text, compared without regard to case, is dropped with fewer than two, and keeps a value only when it is one of them (compared without regard to case, written as the option); a toggle's value is kept only when it is on or off, a date's only when it is YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM naming a real day (year 1 or later, the month's days, leap years) and time (hours to 23, minutes to 59), a number's only when it reads as a number within min and max; min is dropped when it is above max.

A button (an element or an action) needs id for tap and target for open, copy and send, and is dropped without it; a tap button keeps no target and the others keep no id. An open target is kept only when it starts with https://, maps:, tel:, sms:, mailto:, calshow: or x-apple-reminderkit: (compared without regard to case) and holds no spaces, quotes, backticks, backslashes or angle brackets; a send target only when it is a plain message, as a follow-up must be, and a tap button only when its label is one (the tap sends it). A tap button is dropped when the card already has one with that id. A card's first primary button stays primary; the others become plain.
A composed card is dropped when no section is left.

A review's id is kept only when it is rv- and 16 hex digits, and a review without one is dropped. A review's for is kept only when it is W and 1 to 6 digits. A decision is dropped when the review already has one with its id; an option is dropped when its decision already has one with its id. An image option keeps its url only when it is https, and is dropped without one; a page option keeps no url. A decision keeps only its first recommended option, and is dropped with fewer than two options; a review with no decision left is dropped. A settled entry's mark is approve or skip.

layout.description: How the cards are laid out: stack (the default) one under another, or tabs, one card at a time with each card's title as its tab. Conduit picks the columns on wide screens itself.

next.description: Up to four follow-ups the user is likely to ask next, each as the message they would send, in their words, like "Make it $1,500" or "Add a day in Sequoia". Shown under the cards; a tap sends it. Leave it out when nothing obvious comes next.

rules: A follow-up is dropped when it starts with / or !, holds an @ followed by a letter, a digit, an underscore, a slash, a dot or a tilde, or holds a backtick, and only the first of the same follow-ups (compared without regard to case) is kept. This check comes before maxItems, so the first four that pass are kept.

card.description: One card Conduit draws natively. map: a map with a pin per place, and a route when you give one. place: one place in detail. places: several places to swipe through. stats: a few big numbers. chart: a line, bar or pie chart. weather: a forecast. comparison: two to four options side by side. steps: instructions to follow, with timers. media: photos, videos or audio to look at or play. contact: a few people to call, message or email, or someone to text with a message you wrote for the user to send. status: how something in progress is going, like a delivery, a flight, a match or a job. table: rows and columns the user can sort. timeline: a plan by day or phase, each with its stops. checklist: things to tick off, kept across the user's devices. list: a ranked or plain list of things, each with a line and a value. progress: how far along goals are. callout: a tip, note or warning. diff: changes line by line. review: options for the user to look at and mark (a quick pick for one decision, a design review for several), kept on the host. composed: anything else, built from sections of text, metrics, badges, icons, images, progress bars, fields and buttons, like an email ready to send, a day's agenda or an idea to act on.

type.description: The kind of card; fill in its field: places for map, place and places, people for contact, otherwise the field named like the type (options for comparison, sections for composed).

title.description: A short heading, a few words.

live.description: A name for a card you'll keep up to date, like order-4411 or deploy. Show a card with the same live name again in this conversation and it replaces this one wherever it's shown, so give the whole card each time.

source.description: Every type but map, place and places: where the information is from, when it's from a tool, a site or a service rather than your own knowledge. Required for weather and media. Shown on the card.

name.description: Like Open-Meteo, Yahoo Finance or the user's Health data.

places.description: The places, best first. The phone finds each one in Apple Maps itself and shows Apple Maps' address, category, phone, website, travel time and Look Around: don't fill those in. Give coordinates or the place_id from conduit_maps when you have them; otherwise a name and address precise enough to find it.

address.description: Its address or area, to find it.

place_id.description: The Apple Maps place id conduit_maps gave, if any.

note.description: Your own short note on it, shown as yours: why it fits, what to order.

rating.description: Only a rating you actually found, with where it's from. Left out without a source.

source.description: Where it's from, like Google or Yelp.

hours.description: Opening hours you actually found, with where they're from. Left out without a source.

price.description: A price level or price you actually found, with where it's from. Left out without a source.

photo.description: A photo of the place you actually found: a direct image URL, with where it's from. Left out without a source.

route.description: map only: draw a route. Places are counted from 0.

to.description: The place the route goes to.

from.description: The place it starts at. Leave it out to start where the user is.

mode.description: How to travel; driving if left out.

stats.description: stats only: big numbers with labels, most important first.

label.description: What it is, like Steps or Portfolio.

value.description: The number as it should read, with its unit, like 8,412 or $12.4k.

detail.description: A few words under it, like of 10,000 or last 30 days.

tone.description: Whether the change is good news; neutral if left out.

spark.description: Recent values, oldest first, drawn as a small line.

chart.description: chart only: the data, drawn as a native chart.

kind.description: line or area for change over time, bar to compare, pie for shares of a whole.

labels.description: The x-axis labels in order, or a pie's slice names.

series.description: One or more series, each with one value per label. A pie has one.

values.description: One value per label, in order.

unit.description: The values' unit, like %, kg or USD.

weather.description: weather only: a forecast you got from a weather tool or site, never guessed. Give the card's source.

text.description: A few words, like Feels like 21 or Windy later.

precip.description: Chance of rain or snow, in percent.
Chance of rain or snow, in percent.

options.description: comparison only: the options, side by side.

facts.description: Facts to compare, with the same labels in the same order for every option.

pros.description: What's good about it, a few words each.

cons.description: What's not, a few words each.

recommended.description: true on the one you recommend, if any.

needs.description: steps only: what to have ready first, like ingredients or tools.

steps.description: steps only: the steps in order. The user can tick them off.

timer.description: Seconds, when the step waits a set time (simmer 10 minutes is 600): the user can start a timer from it.

media.description: media only: the photos, videos or audio, in order. Only files you actually found, as direct links the phone can load; send a file on this machine as an attachment instead.

url.description: A direct https link to the file or stream (like .jpg, .png, .mp4, .m3u8, .mp3 or .m4a), not a page.

by.description: Who made it: the artist, channel or photographer.

duration.description: video and audio: its length in seconds, if known.

artwork.description: video and audio: a direct link to a still or cover image.

people.description: contact only: the people or businesses. The phone checks each against the user's own contacts and says when one is there; anything else reads as yours.

detail.description: Who they are: a role, a business, or how they're related to the user.

phone.description: A phone number you actually have, with the country code when you know it.

email.description: An email address you actually have.

note.description: Your own short note: why you're showing them.

message.description: A text message you wrote for the user to send them, only when the user asked you to text or message this person. Conduit shows it with a Send text button that opens Messages with it filled in, and the user taps Send there. Needs their phone. It isn't sent until the user taps Send, so never say it was sent.

photo.description: A photo of them you actually found: a direct image URL, with where it's from. Left out without a source; the phone uses the contact's own photo when it has one.

status.description: status only: where something in progress stands. Give it a live name and show it again as it changes.

state.description: Where it stands now, a few words: Out for delivery, Boarding, 2-1 at half time, Building.

phase.description: waiting: not started. active: under way. done: finished. problem: delayed, failed or stuck. active if left out.

progress.description: How far along, from 0 to 1, only when you actually know.

detail.description: A line more: where it is, the score, what's happening.

eta.description: When it should finish or arrive, like 14:20 or in 5 min.

milestones.description: The stages, in order, each done or not yet.

label.description: Like Ordered, Shipped, Out for delivery.

table.description: table only: data in rows and columns. The user can sort by any column. Numbers are fine as text, like $1.2M or 4.5%.

columns.description: The column names, left to right.

rows.description: The rows, each with one cell per column in the same order.

timeline.description: timeline only: the days or phases in order, each with its stops.

label.description: Like Day 1, Fri 12 May or Week 2.

title.description: What the day is about, a few words.

place.description: Where, as a name and area Apple Maps can find, like Glacier Point, Yosemite.

checklist.description: checklist only: things to tick off, like a packing or moving list. Ticks are kept, and you hear which are done when the user changes them. Give it a live name to show it again with changes; ticks stay with items of the same text.

group.description: A heading it goes under, like Clothes or Week before.

list.description: list only: the things, best or first first.

value.description: A number or fact to show beside it, like $2.9T or 4.6.

url.description: A page to open for it.

photo.description: A picture of it you actually found: a direct image URL, with where it's from.

ranked.description: list only: true to number the items as a ranking.

progress.description: progress only: goals and how far along each is.

callout.description: callout only: a short tip, note or warning to stand out.

diff.description: diff only: changes line by line, as the plugin read them from the tool's diff (inputs.diff): the files, each with its hunks, and the lines added and removed in all. Hunks travel with the card only for a short diff; a longer one lists its files, and id names the whole diff kept on the host (GET /boards/diffs).

path.description: The file's path, the new one for a rename.

binary.description: A binary file: no lines to show.

cut.description: Its hunks stop short of all its changes.

context.description: What the diff names after @@, like the function.

lines.description: Each line as the patch has it: + added, - removed, a space unchanged.

id.description: The whole diff, kept on the host.

review.description: review only: options for the user to look at and mark, as the plugin read them from the tool's review (inputs.review). Each option's page is kept on the host (GET /boards/reviews), so the card carries labels and ids; the user marks each decision Approve, Change or Skip and sends the marks, which reach Hermes as their message.

id.description: The review, kept on the host: rv- and 16 hex digits.

round.description: Which round of the review this is.

for.description: The workstream the review belongs to, like W3: the user's marks go to it.

layout.description: side: the options side by side where there's room. switch: one at a time. before_after: two options, the first the before.

kind.description: page: an HTML page kept on the host. image: a picture at url.

settled.description: Decisions an earlier round settled, shown under this round.

sections.description: composed only: the card built from sections, each a row or a column of elements, drawn natively in Conduit's own fonts and colors.

layout.description: column (the default) stacks its elements; row puts them side by side.

more.description: true to fold this section until the user opens the card.

items.description: One element. text: text with a role and tone. metric: a big value with a label. badge: a short tag. icon: an SF Symbol. image: a picture. progress: a bar from 0 to 1. divider: a line. field: something the user fills in, sent with a tap button. button: an action.

text.description: text and badge: what it says.

tone.description: text, metric, badge, icon and progress: neutral if left out.

value.description: metric: the value, like 72% or $1.2M. field: what it starts filled in with (a toggle on or off, a choice one of options, a date a real day as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM).

url.description: image: a direct https image URL you actually found.

input.description: field: what the user fills in.

lines.description: field text: the lines to show, 1 if left out.

placeholder.description: field text: shown while it's empty.

label.description: metric, progress and field: its label. image: what it shows. button: what it says, a verb like Send or Do it.

action.description: open: open target, an https link or a maps:, tel:, sms:, mailto:, calshow: or x-apple-reminderkit: link. copy: copy target. send: send target as the user's message. tap: the user's tap reaches you at once as a message from them, with the card's field values; do it with your tools, then show the card again under its live name with the result.

id.description: tap: what you'll hear was tapped, like send or snooze.

target.description: open: the link. copy: the text. send: the message, in the user's words.

symbol.description: An SF Symbol name, like paperplane.fill.

style.description: plain if left out; one primary at most.

confirm.description: A question Conduit asks before it goes, like Send to Mei?, for anything that sends, buys or deletes.

actions.description: Any card: up to three buttons at its foot.

label.description: What the button says, a verb like Send, Do it or Open in Calendar.

action.description: open: open target, an https link or a maps:, tel:, sms:, mailto:, calshow: or x-apple-reminderkit: link. copy: copy target. send: send target as the user's message. tap: the user's tap reaches you at once as a message from them, with the card's field values; do it with your tools, then show the card again under its live name with the result.

id.description: tap: what you'll hear was tapped, like send or snooze.

target.description: open: the link. copy: the text. send: the message, in the user's words.

symbol.description: An SF Symbol name, like paperplane.fill.

style.description: plain if left out; one primary at most.

confirm.description: A question Conduit asks before it goes, like Send to Mei?, for anything that sends, buys or deletes.

review.description: review only: options for the user to look at and mark, when they're easier to see than to describe. One decision with two to four options is a quick pick the user taps in the chat; several decisions open a review where they mark each Approve, Change or Skip, add notes and send. Give each option an HTML page (html, or file for a page or picture you wrote on the Hermes host) or a picture (image). To show the next round, give the review's id from the earlier card.

id.description: To show the next round of a review: its id (rv-...) from the earlier card. Leave it out to start a review.

for.description: Bot Chat only: the workstream that made the options, like W3. The user's marks go to it, and every round of the review stays with it.

id.description: A short id, like layout; the same id in the next round for the same decision.

text.description: A line on what to look for.

layout.description: side (the default): side by side where there's room. switch: one at a time. before_after: two options, the first the before.

options.description: Two or three is best; more only when they really differ.

text.description: A line on what sets it apart.

recommended.description: The one you'd pick; one at most.

html.description: A whole HTML page showing the option, with its CSS inline; it's shown at phone, tablet or desktop width and in light or dark.

file.description: Instead of html: the absolute path of an .html page or a picture (.png, .jpg, .gif, .webp, .svg) on the Hermes host.

image.description: Instead of html: a direct https link to a picture you actually found.

diff.description: diff only: changes to show line by line, in code, a config or any text: give patch, patch_file, or before and after. Conduit lists the files with the lines added and removed, and the user opens each to read its changes. Put the pull request or commit in source when there is one.

patch.description: A unified diff, as git diff, git show, gh pr diff or diff -u print it: one file or many.

patch_file.description: Instead of patch, for anything longer than a few dozen lines: the absolute path of a file on the Hermes host holding a unified diff, like /tmp/review.diff after git diff main > /tmp/review.diff. Saves writing the diff out.

before.description: With after, for two versions of a text that has no diff: the old one.

name.description: With before and after: the file's name, like nginx.conf.
